about: Maggie's eye, from her test set and her edits on Nov 15 (draft in tests/taste-draft.json). Saved to taste_profiles by scripts/save-taste.ts.

rules.rule: Extra details the original doesn't have (a slit, a pleated bust, ruching, a cut-out) count against a piece only when they change the overall look. When the shape, fabric and proportions are strong, they're a small difference, not a deal-breaker.
The fabric's look carries the piece: prefer fabrics that hang, drape or lie flat the way the original's does. Avoid thin or costume-shiny fabrics.
Keep the original's proportions and length: a short, cinched jacket stays short and cinched, a floor-length gown stays floor-length.
A matching word (velvet, bodysuit, leather) doesn't beat a better look: a piece that gets the look another way can be the better dupe.
The original's own photos and listings, and pieces from the original's own listing pages, aren't dupes.
Embellishment should be fairly literal: beading should read as beading and pearls as pearls. Sequins standing in for beading often, but not always, look cheaper.
For shoes, the toe shape, heel and overall profile should look close to one-for-one. Less literal options are still welcome when the profile matches, such as pebbled instead of smooth leather.

Looks come first. Similar fabric quality is a plus, not a requirement: lining, tailoring or a specific fiber (cashmere, wool, silk) only decides a match when the shopper switches Fabric must match on.
